newsitem.title: USA: West Virginia bill would allow hotel bed tax hike.
newsitem.headline: West Virginia bill would allow hotel bed tax hike.

text.p: A bill pending in the West Virginia House of Delegates would allow cities and counties to raise their hotel bed taxes to six percent to fund convention centers and recreation facilities.
The current limit is three percent. The proposal (HB2545) was undergoing legal review before the House Finance Committee Monday. Sponsors include House Speaker Bob Kiss, D-Raleigh.

Under the bill, the new revenue could only be used for convention centers and recreation facilities. The finance committee added an amendment exempting the dozen or so large hotels that have golf courses.

Motel and hotel industry officials have lobbied against the proposal. City officials in Charleston said that if it passes, they would seek a tax increase to fund renovation at the city's civic center.
